title: Achilles tendon xanthomas + premature CAD family history: check blood cholesterol
vignette: A 31-year-old woman comes to the office for routine check-up. Several subcutaneous bumps seem to be attached to her Achilles tendons. Her father died from a heart attack at age 35 and her mother has rheumatoid arthritis. Her aunt was diagnosed with colon cancer at age 55. Which of the following is the best initial test in this patient?

clues.text: subcutaneous bumps seem to be attached to her Achilles tendons
clues.note: Nodules on the Achilles tendon are TENDINOUS XANTHOMAS - lipid-laden macrophage deposits highly suggestive of hyperlipidemia (familial hypercholesterolemia).

clues.text: father died from a heart attack at age 35
clues.note: Premature coronary death in a first-degree relative supports an inherited severe hypercholesterolemia (autosomal dominant familial hypercholesterolemia).

whatMatters: TENDINOUS XANTHOMAS (Achilles/extensor tendons) plus a family history of PREMATURE cardiac death point to familial HYPERLIPIDEMIA (familial hypercholesterolemia). The best initial test is a BLOOD CHOLESTEROL (lipid) measurement. Answer A.
strategy: Recognize tendinous xanthomas as a marker of hyperlipidemia, then order the test that confirms it: serum cholesterol/lipid panel. Reject the distractors keyed to red-herring family history: fasting glucose (diabetes - acanthosis nigricans, not xanthomas), rheumatoid factor (mother's RA; rheumatoid nodules are on pressure points, not lipid-related), ANA (SLE - not suggested), and fecal occult blood (aunt's colon cancer - screening not indicated by tendon xanthomas).

eliminations.label: Fasting glucose - diabetes shows acanthosis, not xanthomas
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: screening for diabetes/glucose metabolism. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: diabetes-associated skin findings are acanthosis nigricans (and eruptive xanthomas only with very high triglycerides); tendinous xanthomas point to hypercholesterolemia. ✅ Correct if: features of hyperglycemia/insulin resistance.

eliminations.label: Rheumatoid factor - RA nodules differ
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: testing for rheumatoid arthritis (the mother's condition). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: rheumatoid nodules occur on pressure points with joint disease, not lipid-laden tendon xanthomas; RF is a distractor from family history. ✅ Correct if: inflammatory polyarthritis with subcutaneous nodules over pressure points.

eliminations.label: ANA - no lupus features
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: screening for systemic lupus erythematosus. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: nothing suggests an autoimmune connective tissue disease; the finding is xanthomas. ✅ Correct if: malar rash, arthritis, serositis, cytopenias.

eliminations.label: Fecal occult blood - colon cancer screen unrelated
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: screening for GI bleeding/colon cancer (the aunt's diagnosis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: tendon xanthomas indicate hyperlipidemia, not colorectal disease; this is a family-history distractor. ✅ Correct if: colorectal cancer screening by age/risk (not prompted here).

reasoning: Nodules attached to the Achilles tendons are tendinous xanthomas
Tendinous xanthomas indicate hyperlipidemia, especially familial hypercholesterolemia
A father's premature fatal MI supports an inherited severe hypercholesterolemia
-> best initial test is blood cholesterol/lipid panel; answer A
mechanism: XANTHOMAS are deposits of LIPID-LADEN macrophages (foam cells) in skin or tendons, typically associated with HYPERLIPIDEMIA. TENDINOUS XANTHOMAS - firm nodules on the ACHILLES tendon and finger extensor tendons - are characteristic of FAMILIAL HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA, an autosomal dominant LDL-receptor defect that markedly elevates LDL and causes PREMATURE atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (consistent with the father's fatal MI at age 35). Other xanthoma types include eruptive xanthomas (very high triglycerides), plane xanthomas, and xanthelasma (periorbital, often without lipid abnormality). Because the tendon findings and family history point to a lipid disorder, the BEST INITIAL TEST is measurement of serum CHOLESTEROL (lipid panel). The distractors correspond to unrelated conditions cued by the family history (diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, colon cancer).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Path/Biochem > xanthomas: tendinous (Achilles/extensor) = familial hypercholesterolemia (AD LDL receptor defect, premature CAD); eruptive = high triglycerides; xanthelasma = eyelids; work up with lipid panel.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
